title: Richard Cooke to lead Hotel Bel-Air for Dorchester Collection

why: A leader shaped on three continents, with 15+ years at Shangri-La, takes over one of Dorchester Collection's most storied addresses.
body_long:
Dorchester Collection has appointed Richard Cooke general manager of Hotel Bel-Air in Los Angeles, from 1 January 2027. He joins from Rocco Forte Hotels, bringing more than 30 years of international luxury hospitality experience.

Hotel Bel-Air sits within 12 acres of canyon gardens and is one of the most private addresses in Los Angeles. It was recently awarded three Keys by the Michelin Guide, one of only two hotels in the city to hold that rating; the other is its sister property, The Beverly Hills Hotel.

## Three continents

At Rocco Forte Hotels, Richard Cooke was managing director for the UK and Northern Europe. He led operations at Brown's Hotel in London and oversaw the group's hotels in the UK, Belgium and Germany.

Before that, he spent more than 15 years in senior leadership with Shangri-La Hotels & Resorts, including general manager and area general manager roles in Asia and Canada. He began his career in food and beverage management in the United States, with Four Seasons, Regent, Ritz-Carlton and Rosewood. Born and raised in the UK, he completed the general manager programme at Singapore Management University and executive education at the Cornell-Nanyang Institute of Hospitality.

Philippe Leboeuf, CEO of Dorchester Collection, described Hotel Bel-Air as unlike anywhere else, with a loyal following and a creative team, and praised Cooke's warmth and cosmopolitan outlook. Cooke said he was proud to join the group and glad to return to California, where his family is based.

## The signal

Dorchester Collection is entrusting one of its most storied addresses to a leader shaped on three continents. For a heritage icon with a loyal clientele, that breadth matters as much as the history: the job is to keep what guests love while preparing the hotel for its next decade.

Congratulations to Richard Cooke on this new chapter.
